name: Life Code
voice: Scientific, credible and trustworthy — a longevity-science nutraceutical brand. Confident about the research and the formulation, but disciplined and compliant in how benefits are stated (structure/function language, never disease claims). Speaks to informed adults who take healthy aging seriously: clear, evidence-forward, premium, calm. No hype, no miracle tone.
photo_rules: CLEAN, SCIENTIFIC, PREMIUM — white space, navy #14294D as the anchor colour, a disciplined red #C8202F only for one accent/CTA element, soft light-blue #EEF2F8 panels. HERO: the bottle, front-facing, label readable, crisp studio light. Use REAL botanical ingredients as supporting props (Astragalus root, Rhodiola, Gotu Kola, Ashwagandha, Schisandra, Pine Bark, Milk Thistle) and clean, STYLISED science visuals (a cell, a telomere/chromosome motif, a pathway diagram) — abstract and elegant, NOT clinical/medical or scary. PROVE trust with badge rows buyers scan for: Made in USA · GMP / cGMP facility · Laboratory Tested · 100% Vegetarian Capsules · Non-GMO where true · 90-Day Money-Back Guarantee. Lifestyle = active, healthy, vibrant mature adults (50s-70s) living well — hiking, cooking, with grandkids — NEVER sick/before-after/medical imagery. Ingredient-and-mechanism infographics that stay honest. English overlays, PUNCHY (<=5 words), one idea per image.
no_gos: COMPLIANCE IS THE #1 RULE (US dietary supplement / Amazon). NEVER claim to cure, treat, prevent, reverse or diagnose any disease or aging itself. Do NOT state as literal fact that the product 'lengthens telomeres', 'activates/increases stem cells', 'regenerates cells', 'reverses aging', 'extends life/lifespan' or 'anti-aging' as a promised outcome — use hedged STRUCTURE/FUNCTION wording exactly like the live Amazon listings: 'designed to support', 'formulated to support telomere-related pathways', 'supports healthy aging', 'supports cellular health / longevity pathways'. No 'clinically proven', 'doctor-recommended', 'FDA-approved', 'guaranteed results', 'best/#1'. No disease names, no medical/scary imagery, no before/after, no lab-coat doctor implying medical treatment. No prices/URLs on-image (the 90-day guarantee badge is fine). The DTC site (lifecoderx.com) uses more aggressive claims (Stem Cell Activation, Regeneration, Life Extension) — DO NOT copy those onto Amazon creative.
